sections.html:
Tucker owners can list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a direct offer from a buyer who purchases houses in their current condition. The city sits inside DeKalb County, so assessment, tax billing and deed recording for any sale run through county offices.

  • An agent listing reaches the most buyers, though showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage approval stretch the calendar.
  • A sale by owner keeps price and terms in your hands, along with the contract and disclosure work.
  • A direct buyer skips financing contingencies and repair requests, and the offer usually lands below a fully renovated listing price.

Whichever way you go, collect the deed, your mortgage payoff figure, any open permit paperwork and HOA covenants before the first conversation. Most of the delay in a Georgia sale comes from documents that could have been prepared in advance.

sections.h2: Is your address in the city?
sections.html:
Tucker has widened its borders since 2016, which is unusual for a metro Atlanta city. Land area grew from 11.98 square miles in 2010 to 20.20 square miles in 2020. Homeowners along Livsey Drive petitioned to join in September 2016, and the Wanda Woods and Westwood subdivisions followed on January 1, 2017. Briarcliff Village Shopping Center was annexed in 2018, and a year later much of the neighboring Northlake Mall came in too.

A petition needs property touching the current boundary, and the mayor and council must approve it by majority vote. For a seller, the practical point is that your street may sit just across a line. Confirm whether the house is in the city or in unincorporated DeKalb County, because that decides which permit desk and code officers you deal with.

Owners live in 63.0 percent of Tucker's homes. Unless a label gives a date, each figure below is a 2020 to 2024 estimate.

A middle value describes the whole city, so your own number turns on condition, lot size and street. Buyers will compare your house with nearby sales, not with the citywide figure.

Tucker's cluster schools belong to the DeKalb County School District. Five neighborhood elementary schools feed Tucker Middle School, and Tucker Middle feeds Tucker High School, which has won state football and basketball championships. The district has been running a student assignment project, so zones may shift. Check the assigned schools for your exact address with the district office before you put anything about schools in writing.

  • Look up the attendance zone for your address on the district site.
  • Name the cluster in your listing or your pitch to a buyer.
  • Keep a copy of the zone confirmation in your sale file.

sections.h2: Permits, code rules and business licenses
sections.html:
Unpermitted work, code violations and covenant restrictions cause most hiccups. Tucker's Building and Permitting Division reviews plans, issues permits and conducts inspections, and permits can be submitted electronically.

The city lists water heater replacement, water or sewer line replacement, electrical service upgrades, panel changes and air conditioner change outs as work that needs a permit. Paint, minor non-structural repairs such as glass panes and door hardware, and detached non-habitable structures under 200 square feet do not. Subdivision covenants may still apply, so ask your homeowners association first.

Code Enforcement aims for voluntary compliance. Typical examples are an inoperable vehicle parked on private property and outdoor storage, both of which can be fixed in a weekend before a buyer walks through.

If you run a business from the house, the city requires an occupational tax certificate for every for-profit business, home-based ones included. Renewals fall due January 1 and turn delinquent after April 15. The licensing line at City Hall is (678) 597-9040.

sections.h2: How to appeal your DeKalb valuation
sections.html:
DeKalb sets a value as of January 1 each year and taxes 40 percent of fair market value. Once the notice goes out, you have 45 days to appeal.

The county's property search tool displays current and past values, lets you download notices, and accepts an online appeal using the access code from your notice. A mailed appeal goes to the Property Appraisal Department, 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, and should include the parcel number, your reason, your evidence and which appeal route you choose.

  • Board of Equalization: free, heard by a three-member panel of property owners.
  • Hearing Officer: for properties over $500,000 that are not homesteaded, with no filing fee.
  • Non-binding arbitration: needs a certified appraisal you pay for, plus a $217 filing fee.

The appeal matters to a seller while you still hold title, because the buyer inherits the final value. Bills themselves come from the DeKalb Tax Commissioner's Office.

sections.h2: Closing, transfer tax and land use
sections.html:
Georgia will not let a deed be recorded until its transfer tax is paid, and the Department of Revenue page prints the rate. The seller owes it by default, and the contract may move it to the buyer. The declaration is Form PT-61, filed online through the clerks' cooperative authority, whose support lines are (800) 304-5174 and (404) 327-9760. For exemption questions, the state sends you to the county clerk.

Land use questions have their own channel. Tucker has a Planning Commission, a Zoning Board of Appeals and a Construction Board of Appeals, plus a land use petition directory for rezoning and variance requests. Ask Planning and Zoning at (678) 597-9040 before promising a buyer that a lot can be split or a use changed.

In a cash sale there is no lender appraisal or loan underwriting to wait on, so the closing steps are the title search, the payoff, the PT-61 and the recording.

faqs.q: Is it possible to sell a Tucker house that needs work?
faqs.a: Yes. Sell it as is, hand it to an investor, or fix only the items that would block a buyer's loan. Open permits and unpermitted work are the problems most likely to surface, so check them with the city's Building and Permitting Division first.

faqs.q: Does replacing a water heater in Tucker need a permit?
faqs.a: Yes. The city names water heater replacement among its mechanical, electrical and plumbing permit examples. Have the contractor pull the permit so the inspection record is ready when a buyer asks.

faqs.q: Who owes the Georgia transfer tax in a Tucker sale?
faqs.a: State law makes the seller liable, though sales contracts often assign it to the buyer. Read that clause before signing, since the amount is set by the price and is due before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: How much time does a DeKalb owner get to contest a value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the date printed on the notice. File through the county property search with the notice's access code, or mail a written appeal to the Property Appraisal Department in Decatur.

faqs.q: Are all Tucker-area addresses inside the city?
faqs.a: No. The city has annexed neighborhoods and commercial areas since 2016, and nearby addresses may still be in unincorporated DeKalb County. City Hall or the city map will tell you which side of the line your house is on.
